newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN rejects Elf's Iraq oil contract on technicality.
newsitem.headline: UN rejects Elf's Iraq oil contract on technicality.

text.p: U.N.-appointed overseers charged with reviewing all oil contracts under the Iraqi oil-for-food plan, rejected a deal Tuesday between France's Elf-Aquitaine and Iraq, U.N. sources said.
Overseers denied the second contract submitted under the oil plan on technical grounds.
"One application was rejected because SOMO (Iraq's State Oil and Marketing Organization) posted the contract directly to the United Nations, not through the mission," said a diplomat.
There was no problem with the contract itself, just the technical manner in which it was delivered, the diplomat added.
Elf was not immediately available for comment.
The first contract submitted, but yet to be approved by the overseers, was between SOMO and the Turkish company Tapras for 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil for six months.
Additionally, a United Nations spokesman confirmed oil flows were stopped Tuesday for technical reasons.
Under the oil for aid accord signed May 20 and cleared for service Monday, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude over a six-month period.
The partial lifting of sanctions will allow Iraq to buy food and supplies for civilians suffering from sanctions imposed on Baghdad after it invaded Kuwait in 1990.
Around two-thirds of the oil revenues were earmarked for needy Iraqis, and the balance for Gulf war reparations and related monitoring costs.
